newsitem.title: USA: Cargill team leaves North Korea without agreement.
newsitem.headline: Cargill team leaves North Korea without agreement.

text.p: A Cargill Inc team negotiating in North Korea last week over the financing of a recently approved grain shipment to that drought-stricken nation left Pyongyang this past weekend without an agreement, a Cargill spokesperson said Monday.
"They left this weekend without agreement," said Lori Johnson of Cargill. "We're continuing to work toward an agrement."
Cargill was given recent approval to ship 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice to North Korea. The undecided issues involve financing and how much of each commodity Korea wants.
Johnson would not comment on what the stumbling blocks are in the talks, but said it is not significant that the meetings are no longer being held face to face.
She said Cargill officials remain in contact with North Korean officials.
"There were Cargill officials there from all over the world that have other responsibilities...grain trade negotiations are often not conducted face to face," she said.

In a possibly related development, U.S. State Department announced Monday a briefing with North Korea on a proposal for Korean peninsula peace talks has been postponed until Feb 5 in New York because North Korea wanted to complete grain negotiations with a "private western company," presumably Cargill.

In reaction to Cargill's possible impact on the diplomatic talks, Johnson said, "We're not a part of -- in any way, shape or form -- the diplomatic negotiations going on between the various governments. In our minds it is a commercial deal and is wholly separate from the diplomatic negotiations that do not include us."
There were unconfirmed reports that North Korea was asking the U.S. government to help finance the Cargill shipment, but Johnson said she was unaware of such a request.
